data.narrative:
Karman Industries is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by David Tearse and Chiranjeev Kalra. The company has raised $11.5M to date. The valuation universe comprises 8 private peers in Climate & Energy alongside 1 public comparable (LNZA), though direct peer-set filtering yielded insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage matches for reliable median-based analysis.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach here. Using total capital raised ($11.5M, rounded to $12M as a proxy for post-money valuation floor) and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Seed to Series A, the method yields an implied valuation of $29M. This reflects the expected value accretion between capital rounds absent company-specific operational milestones or burn metrics.

Given the single-method foundation, the triangulated valuation range is $24M (low) to $33M (high), centered on $29M. The range reflects ±15% variance around the median to account for execution risk, path-dependency on near-term technical or commercial de-risking, and the absence of tighter peer comparability. Key uncertainties include Karman's unit economics trajectory, capital efficiency relative to sector norms, and clarity on technology differentiation within the crowded frontier-energy landscape. A subsequent valuation update will require either comparable transaction data from the narrower peer set or improved visibility into the company's go-to-market traction.
